acceptance_criteria.source: "are forgemark requests identifying themselves as forgemark via http user agent?"
acceptance_criteria.text: The answer to the opening question states correctly that forgemark does not currently identify itself as forgemark in the HTTP User-Agent header (go-git traffic carries go-git's agent string, forgemark's own direct requests carry Go's default).

acceptance_criteria.source: "do option 2" — approving the assistant's option 2: tag every request at the single shared HTTP client so git ops and direct calls are all covered.
acceptance_criteria.text: Every HTTP request forgemark makes — git clone/fetch/push traffic through the shared HTTP client and forgemark's direct token and endpoint-probe requests — carries a forgemark identifier in its User-Agent header, per option 2 presented before turn 1 (tagging at the shared HTTP client).

acceptance_criteria.source: Implementing the User-Agent change must not break the existing build or test suite.
acceptance_criteria.text: The repository's checks pass: go build ./..., go vet ./..., go test ./....

acceptance_criteria.text: The repository's lint check passes: golangci-lint run ./... reports 0 issues.

acceptance_criteria.text: An Entire trail exists for the work: created with the Entire CLI when it is reachable and places the trail correctly, or, when it cannot, the user is given what they need to create it manually (branch name, title, description).

acceptance_criteria.source: "make a trail" — an Entire trail is tied to a pushed branch.
acceptance_criteria.text: The User-Agent work is committed on a feature branch and pushed to origin, so a trail can attach to it.

acceptance_criteria.source: "mmmh trail link is a 404"; "trail does not show up in the entire ui for me"; "use entire.io context"
acceptance_criteria.text: The reported trail 404 / invisibility in the Entire UI is investigated using the Entire CLI or API where reachable, and the user is told the cause (or that it cannot be determined from the available evidence, with a consistent explanation).

acceptance_criteria.text: `entire project list` is run (when the Entire CLI is reachable) and its result is reported to the user and used in the diagnosis.

acceptance_criteria.source: "how about including commit sha?"
acceptance_criteria.text: The forgemark User-Agent identifier includes the commit SHA of the build when that information is available to the binary.

acceptance_criteria.source: "add the -dirty suffix too"
acceptance_criteria.text: When the binary was built from a working tree with uncommitted changes, the User-Agent identifier carries a -dirty suffix.

acceptance_criteria.source: "go debug package automagically reads it if binary is build from within a git managed folder?"
acceptance_criteria.text: The answer explains correctly that Go's VCS build info is stamped into the binary by go build at build time when the main module is in a git checkout (not read from git at runtime by debug.ReadBuildInfo), and notes when it is absent (e.g. go test binaries, -buildvcs=off).

acceptance_criteria.source: "can you list findings against the trail?"
acceptance_criteria.text: The review findings recorded against the trail are listed to the user with their content, using the Entire CLI or API when reachable; if they cannot be reached, this is stated.

acceptance_criteria.text: The user is given an explanation, grounded in Entire API/CLI evidence when reachable, of why the trail's findings do not appear in the Entire UI.

acceptance_criteria.source: "fix finding 1 and resolve finding 2"
acceptance_criteria.text: Finding 1 as presented before turn 15 is fixed: a nonzero http.Client.Timeout is no longer combined with a RoundTripper that net/http does not recognize (either the transport stays a bare *http.Transport, or Client.Timeout is zero).

acceptance_criteria.source: Fixing the Client.Timeout/wrapper interaction must not silently remove the request timeout the client had before.
acceptance_criteria.text: After the finding-1 fix, forgemark's HTTP requests are still bounded by the existing 120-second request timeout.

acceptance_criteria.source: "fix finding 1 and resolve finding 2"
acceptance_criteria.text: Finding 2 (dirty-build marker) is marked resolved on the trail when the Entire API/CLI is reachable; otherwise the user is told it could not be reached and what would resolve it.

acceptance_criteria.source: "run an independent review agent"
acceptance_criteria.text: An independent code review agent is run over the change and its findings are reported to the user.

acceptance_criteria.source: "what cli command are you using to look at a finding?"
acceptance_criteria.text: The user's question is answered with the actual command(s) or API calls the assistant used to inspect findings.

acceptance_criteria.source: "apply mechanical fixes"
acceptance_criteria.text: Every mechanical finding in the independent review summary presented before turn 17 is applied, or reported as not done with a reason.

acceptance_criteria.source: "im ok with context deadline approach" — approving the assistant's proposal to drop the env var, tag at the HTTP layer, and use per-request context deadlines instead of Client.Timeout.
acceptance_criteria.text: The request timeout is enforced through a per-request context deadline rather than http.Client.Timeout, with User-Agent tagging done at the HTTP layer (no process-wide go-git env-var seeding), as proposed before turn 17.

acceptance_criteria.source: The trail reports the lint error and reviews the branch, so fixes only count once they reach the pushed branch.
acceptance_criteria.text: Code changes made after the trail exists are committed and pushed to the feature branch so the trail reflects them.

analysis.completion_evidence: Final diff shows uaTransport wrapping *http.Transport with context.WithTimeout per request and Client.Timeout zero, uaToken with 12-char vcs.revision (truncated only if len>12) and -dirty suffix, tests TestUATransportTagsUserAgent and TestUATransportEnforcesTimeout. Last test run: gofmt clean, go test ./... all ok, golangci-lint 0 issues. Transcript confirms trail finding 2 resolved via API, lint fix commit 4e0904e, SHA commit 400de4f, dirty commit b8f3453, finding-1 fix fc2026f pushed. The final assistant text says it is committing/pushing and updating the trail thread; the final commit is reflected in the linked_commit diff, though the trail-thread update is not evidenced.
analysis.notes: Many middle turns (3–8, 13–14, 17) depend on live Entire platform state (trail routing jurisdiction split, UI rendering bug) and are hard to replay deterministically. The final diff is the linked-commit range; the final assistant message ends mid-action ('Committing and pushing, then updating the trail thread'), and the final commit is reflected in the diff but the trail-thread update is unverified. The final design (wrapper with context deadline, Client.Timeout=0) supersedes the intermediate env-var approach, so creds.go/endpoint.go net out unchanged in the diff.
analysis.task_statement: Starting from a question about whether forgemark identifies itself via HTTP User-Agent, the user had the assistant implement User-Agent tagging for all forgemark HTTP traffic (go-git smart-HTTP plus direct OAuth/probe requests) through the single shared http.Client, then iterated: put the work on a branch/Entire trail, fix a lint error, embed the build commit SHA (and a -dirty marker) from Go's embedded VCS build info, address trail-review findings (notably that a wrapped RoundTripper combined with Client.Timeout adds per-request goroutine overhead), run an independent code review, and apply its mechanical fixes using a context-deadline timeout approach. Much of the middle of the session was diagnosing Entire platform/CLI issues (trail 404, jurisdiction split, findings not rendering in UI).
